clue.text: An aerial I'd erected 5½ yards long

indicators.note: in a down clue, erected means the letters are stood upright, read from the bottom up

parts.note: I'd is written ID without the apostrophe
a pole, like a rod or perch, is an old measure of five and a half yards

explanation.surface: Someone puts up a very long TV aerial in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erected' turns ID upwards to DI; the pole is the old imperial length unit, five and a half yards.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-rod antenna fed at its centre is the basic radio receiver of that design.

clue.text: Space-traveller is a bodybuilder?

parts.note: an anabolic steroid builds muscle, so it is literally a body builder

explanation.surface: A muscleman is asked whether he is a space traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bodybuilder' suggests a gym-goer, but here it is the drug that builds the body.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor planet orbiting the sun travels through space.

clue.text: Groundless projects for rooks on the wing?

parts.note: in chess the rook is also called the castle
birds on the wing are flying, up aloft

explanation.surface: Rooks, the black birds, are pictured flying about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rooks' looks like the birds, which fits 'on the wing', but it is the chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Daydream schemes with no foundation are idiomatically fantasy fortresses floating aloft.

clue.text: Busy on redaction, I'd get in a 25

indicators.note: 25 across is a word for a confused mass, so being in a muddle tells us these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An editor working on a redacted document admits getting into a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a 25' refers to the answer at 25 across, a muddle, signalling an anagram of the seven letters of I'D GET IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone occupied with revising and cutting text is said to be at work preparing copy.

clue.text: Fairly generous personal move made in a friendly game?

definitions.text: Fairly generous personal move made in a friendly game?

parts.words: Fairly generous personal move made in a friendly game?
parts.note: a magnanimous act that plays fair, such as kicking the ball out for an injured opponent in a match

explanation.definitionFit: A gracious act of fair play by a competitor shows good sportsmanship.

clue.text: Twin skylights

parts.note: skylights read as lights in the sky, the stars of a constellation named for twins

explanation.definitionFit: The zodiac constellation of Castor and Pollux represents the twins.

clue.text: I get taken in by the lady's successor

indicators.note: taken in by means the letter I goes inside the word for the lady's

parts.note: the lady's, as a possessive, is her

explanation.surface: Someone is taken in by a woman who becomes their successor.
explanation.definitionFit: One who inherits a title or property succeeds to it.

clue.text: The trivia of a coin collection?

definitions.meaning: odds and ends, small unimportant things
a bit and a piece are both old words for a coin, as in a threepenny bit

explanation.definitionFit: Odds and ends are trifles; a pile of threepenny coins and sixpenny coins is literally a heap of change.

clue.text: See 8
See 8
Powerful new poet not without heart

indicators.note: new means the letters of poet are made into something fresh, rearranged
without heart means the middle letter of not is dropped, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: A poet is said to be powerful, though not heartless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges POET to POTE; 'without heart' takes the middle O from NOT, leaving NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong and forceful in effect, like a strong drug.

clue.text: Rows about stray dogs

indicators.note: about means the word for rows goes around the word for stray

parts.note: tiers are rows, as of seats in a stadium
to err is to stray from the right path

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rows' looks like quarrels, but it means rows of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Small hunting breeds such as the Jack Russell belong to this group of canines.

clue.text: Disappear, as problems do when one shuts one's eyes to them

definitions.text: as problems do when one shuts one's eyes to them
definitions.meaning: ignoring a difficulty means you no longer see it, though it remains

explanation.definitionFit: Vanishing means passing out of sight; ignored troubles seem gone because they cannot be seen.

clue.text: In April it is set fire to

indicators.note: In tells us the answer sits inside the words that follow, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: Something is set alight in April.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignited, past tense of light, means kindled.

clue.text: American apple of premier importance to us in the 30s

definitions.meaning: a red American dessert apple variety

definitions.text: premier importance to us in the 30s
definitions.meaning: Stanley ... was Britain's Prime Minister (premier) in the 1930s

explanation.definitionFit: The name is both a US apple cultivar and the Conservative prime minister of the 1930s.

clue.text: A turn gone by

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game

explanation.definitionFit: Past, earlier than now, as in 'years before'.

clue.text: The nimbleness displayed by a U S soldier amid the ruins of Italy

indicators.note: amid means the soldier's letters are placed among the jumbled letters
the ruins of means the letters of Italy are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: GI is the usual term for an American soldier

explanation.surface: A nimble American soldier picks his way through Italian ruins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the ruins of' scrambles the country's name to ALITY; 'amid' slips the American soldier in just after its opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Quickness and lightness of movement is a synonym of nimbleness.

clue.text: The French Venerable turns red then lilac

parts.note: la is French for the (feminine)
Ven is the abbreviation for Venerable, an archdeacon's title

indicators.note: turns means the word red is reversed

explanation.surface: A French archdeacon blushes red and then pale purple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' reverses RED to DER; the Venerable is the Church of England title of an archdeacon, abbreviated Ven.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale purple colour, the shade of lilac blossom.

clue.text: School girl embracing blackguard from the Orient

indicators.note: embracing means the girl's name surrounds the other letters

parts.note: Amy is a girl's name
a cad is a dishonourable man
E is short for East, the Orient

explanation.surface: A schoolgirl is attached to a scoundrel from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Orient' gives E (East), a crossword convention; 'embracing' wraps the girl's name round the scoundrel plus that E.
explanation.definitionFit: An institution of learning, such as a military or performing-arts college.

clue.text: Not however the sort of work for which the household troops are trained

definitions.text: Not however the sort of work for which the household troops are trained

parts.words: Not however the sort of work for which the household troops are trained
parts.note: household troops are guards regiments, but the clue reads them as the staff of a home, cooks and maids

explanation.definitionFit: Working as a servant in a private home, as maids and butlers do.

clue.text: No longer in a fit state to breathe out?

parts.note: ex means former, no longer
hale means healthy, fit

explanation.surface: Someone no longer fit enough to breathe out.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel air from the lungs is the opposite of inhaling.

clue.text: Material feature of a typical iconoclast

indicators.note: feature of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A trait typical of a rebel who smashes images.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain-woven cotton cloth is a fabric.

clue.text: He comes in to see to things in the finish

indicators.note: comes in means the word he is put inside the following phrase

parts.note: to attend to something is to see to it

explanation.surface: A man arrives to deal with matters at the close.
explanation.definitionFit: Finally, at the conclusion.

clue.text: Unexciting meat dish

indicators.note: dish as a verb means to ruin or mess up, so the letters of meat are scrambled

explanation.walkthrough: 'dish' looks like a noun for food, but it is a verb signalling a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Dull and lacking excitement, as a domesticated animal is docile.

clue.text: Confused mass of coarse seaweed

definitions.meaning: a knot or muddle of threads

explanation.definitionFit: Both a snarl of threads and a large brown kelp share this name.

clue.text: A distorted film about a seaside resort in Italy

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go around the second a
distorted means the letters of film are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A warped film is made about a holiday town in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distorted' rearranges FILM to MLFI, and 'about' puts it around A to give MALFI, after the first A.
explanation.definitionFit: A coastal town in Campania on the famous coast south of Naples.

clue.text: A gate-crasher coming back for spoil

indicators.note: coming back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a battering ram crashes through gates

explanation.surface: A party gate-crasher returns to ruin things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gate-crasher' suggests an uninvited guest, but it is a battering ram.
explanation.definitionFit: To damage or blemish, as to ruin a perfect record.

clue.text: Every peach gone soft

indicators.note: gone means the letter for soft has departed from the fruit

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical abbreviation for soft

explanation.walkthrough: 'gone soft' looks like ripe fruit, but P (piano, soft in music) is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Each one of a group, all individually.
